claim: For \(T>0\), let \(0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T\) be a partition with widths \(h_i=t_{i+1}-t_i>0\), let \(A_i\) be IID real actions independent of a Brownian motion \(W\), and set \(Z=A^2\), \(q=\mathbb E Z<\infty\). On interval \([t_i,t_{i+1})\), the sampled model is \(dX_t^\pi=A_i\,dW_t\), while the aggregated model is \(d\widetilde X_t=\sqrt q\,dW_t\), both started at zero. With \(\ell(s)=\mathbb E e^{-sZ}\), their terminal characteristic functions are \(\mathbb E e^{iuX_T^\pi}=\prod_i\ell(u^2h_i/2)\) and \(\mathbb E e^{iu\widetilde X_T}=e^{-u^2qT/2}\). For every \(u\ne0\), the sampled characteristic function is strictly larger than the aggregated one exactly when \(Z\) is nonconstant; the entire process laws agree exactly when \(A^2\) is almost surely constant, even if the common-Brownian strong error is nonzero. For fixed \(N,T\), the uniform partition uniquely minimizes the characteristic-function excess at every \(u\ne0\) when \(Z\) is nonconstant. If \(\mathbb E A^4<\infty\), the exact fourth-moment excess is \(3\operatorname{Var}(A^2)\sum_i h_i^2\), uniquely minimized by the uniform grid at \(3T^2\operatorname{Var}(A^2)/N\). More generally, for each \(k\ge1\) with \(\mathbb E|A|^{2k}<\infty\), the terminal even moment of order \(2k\) is minimized by the uniform grid. For \(f\in C_b^6\), \(q>0\), and \(\mathbb E Z^3<\infty\), the weak-bias expansion is \(\mathbb E f(X_T^\pi)-\mathbb E f(\widetilde X_T)=\frac{\operatorname{Var}(Z)}8\left(\sum_i h_i^2\right)\mathbb E f^{(4)}(\widetilde X_T)+R_\pi\), with \(|R_\pi|\le\|f^{(6)}\|_\infty\mathbb E|\sum_i h_i(Z_i-q)|^3/48\).

correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the IID actions yields the exact Gaussian variance mixture \(V_\pi=\sum_i h_iZ_i\). Jensen gives the strict characteristic-function comparison and its equality condition. Strict convexity of \(s\mapsto\log\mathbb E[e^{-sZ}]\) proves the uniform-grid minimum. Conditional Gaussian moments give the exact fourth-moment identity; symmetry, convexity, and majorization prove the all-even-moment minimization. Taylor expansion of \(H(v)=\mathbb E[f(\sqrt vG)]\), with \(H''(v)= rac14\mathbb E[f^{(4)}(\sqrt vG)]\) and \(\|H'''\|_\infty\le\|f^{(6)}\|_\infty/8\), gives the stated weak-bias coefficient and remainder. The deterministic script was run and passed its listed finite checks.
